instruction:
You are tasked with designing a distance module in Verilog that calculates the Euclidean distance between two cities represented by their Cartesian coordinates. The module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs:
- clk: clock signal
- rst: reset signal
- citya: 64-bit input representing the Cartesian coordinates of city A in the format {y[31:0], x[31:0]}
- cityb: 64-bit input representing the Cartesian coordinates of city B in the format {y[31:0], x[31:0]}
- inp_valid: input valid signal indicating when new city coordinates are available

Outputs:
- out_valid: output valid signal indicating when the calculated distance is available
- out: 32-bit output representing the Euclidean distance between city A and city B

The module should use the cordic_sqrt module to compute the square root of the distance. The cordic_sqrt module has the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs:
- aclk: clock signal
- s_axis_cartesian_tvalid: input valid signal indicating when a new input is available
- s_axis_cartesian_tdata: 24-bit input representing the squared distance between city A and city B
- m_axis_dout_tvalid: output valid signal indicating when the square root is available
- m_axis_dout_tdata: 16-bit output representing the square root of the input

You can assume that the input coordinates are always valid and that the distance between the cities will not exceed 2^31-1.
